script.opening_words: Have you ever noticed that the person who barely passed high school is now driving a Tesla while your valedictorian friend is still complaining about student loan payments? Yeah, me too. And honestly, it used to drive me absolutely crazy. I mean, where's the justice in that? Shouldn't the smartest people automatically end up with the most money? Uh-huh. Well, turns out the universe has a twisted sense of humor, and intelligence doesn't work the way we think it does
script.ending_words: returns, not on how impressive they'll make you sound at parties. So, there you have it. While geniuses are busy overthinking and protecting their reputation, regular folks are out there building wealth through persistence, action, and good old-fashioned people skills. Maybe it's time to embrace being average and start getting rich.
script.analysis: Full 19633 canonical characters read. A contrarian mindset essay: hook (average student with a Tesla), Swedish ability-plateau study, five reasons - stupid grit (persistence, consistent investing), action over analysis (lawn-care friend), emotional intelligence, no fear of looking stupid (Pet Rock, cat drawings), and avoiding prestige spending (Ivy vs state school, plumber vs engineers) - and a habits close. Verified: the Swedish study design and top-1% finding (ESR 2023). Overstated/unsupported: top earners "a little bit dumber" (they are above average, only slightly below the next stratum); EQ "85-90% of success" (popular misquote); Ivy sticker-price comparison ignores aid; plumber/engineer anecdote unrepresentative. Few numeric claims; the cat-drawing revenue needs merchandise to reach $300K. The stored ending is complete.

claim_audit.claim: Swedish researchers followed ~60,000 conscripted men with register wage data; ability rose with pay until ~$55,000, then the link fell apart; the top 1% scored slightly lower.
claim_audit.stored_text_witness:

claim_audit.assessment: SWEIQ2023: Keuschnigg, van de Rijt & Bol, European Sociological Review (2023): 59,000 Swedish conscripted men; ability plateaus at ~+1 SD above ~EUR60,000/year; top 1% score slightly lower than the stratum just below (verified via university/press summaries). The script's "$55,000" and "11 years" are not confirmed; the finding is a plateau, not that the top earners are "dumber" than average - they remain well above average, which the script partly acknowledges. Men in Sweden only.
